writeup: TIC 231055671 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry data with an orbital period of 30.523 days. The primary eclipse produces a 32.57% dimming, while a secondary eclipse appears at a 7.5 sigma detection level. Automated analysis achieved a detection signal-to-noise of 652.2 using the Box Least Squares algorithm, and pixel-level imaging confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 134.8, though the centroid offset of 2.7 arcsec from the target requires consideration. The system does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, a data quality analysis revealed that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the true orbital period may be double the initially measured value. This anomaly points to either instrumental effects or genuine period-doubling behavior that warrants further investigation.
